sections.h2: How does the village and town split affect a Greenburgh home sale?
sections.html:
Which offices handle your sale depends on whether the house is in one of the town's six villages or in the unincorporated area. Greenburgh lies in western Westchester County. The Hudson River forms its western edge, Yonkers lies south, Mount Pleasant north, and White Plains and Scarsdale to the east.

Wikipedia's entry on Greenburgh gives the founding year as 1788 and the land area as about 30 of its 36 square miles, with 95,397 people counted in 2020. About half of them live inside villages. The remainder live in unincorporated pockets such as the Fairview, Greenville and Hartsdale census areas, plus North Elmsford and South Ardsley.

The town Building Department says it takes complaints only for the unincorporated part of Greenburgh, and the Tax Department sends village residents to their own Village Hall for due dates. So a seller in Tarrytown has two sets of offices to check, while a seller in Hartsdale deals mainly with the town.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Greenburgh housing costs?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's profile puts the median value of owner-occupied homes at $697,100 for 2020 to 2024, a level where closing costs and the state's one percent high-value threshold start to matter. The figures below come from that profile.

A commute of that length fits a town where rail service into the city is a main draw. At $2,316 a month, median rent is a useful yardstick if you are weighing a sale against keeping the house as a rental. About a quarter of residents were born abroad (24.3 percent), and 30.6 percent of people age five and over speak another language at home, so listing materials in more than one language can widen the audience.

sections.h2: Which trains, roads and schools do Greenburgh buyers ask about?
sections.html:
• Trains: Metro-North's Hudson Line stops in Hastings-on-Hudson, Dobbs Ferry, Ardsley-on-Hudson, Irvington and Tarrytown. The Harlem Line has a Hartsdale station.
  • Highways: the Thruway, the Cross Westchester Expressway, and the Saw Mill River, Bronx River and Sprain Brook parkways all pass through, along with US 9 and state routes 9A, 100 and 119.
  • Buses: the county's Bee-Line system runs in town.
  • Schools: the tax office bills for ten separate school districts, so the district on your bill is the first thing most buyers check.

Since the district changes the total tax bill from one street to the next, pull your current bill before you set a price.

sections.h2: Which Greenburgh building rules should you check before listing?
sections.html:
The Building Department's FAQ says a permit is needed for any construction, repair, improvement, modification or demolition. A re-roof on a one or two family house counts, and structural roof changes need drawings sealed by a New York State architect or engineer.

  • Sheds of every size need a permit. The limit is one per lot, in the rear yard, at 150 square feet and 10 feet high at most.
  • A fence needs no building permit up to six feet in a front or side yard and eight feet in the rear, with a 30 inch cap near corners.
  • Repaving an existing driveway needs no permit, but enlarging it does, and Public Works may also require a curb cut or right-of-way permit.
  • Pulling or abandoning a heating oil tank takes its own permit and inspection.
  • No residential zoning district lists short-term rentals as a permitted use.

That last rule matters when a buyer plans a vacation rental. The department's forms page says applications are taken in person or by mail on weekdays at 177 Hillside Avenue, and it posts its current hours there.

sections.h2: How are Greenburgh property taxes collected and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes bills for the county, the town, the fire districts and ten school districts, a total the Tax Department page puts above a quarter billion dollars a year. It describes the office as the largest municipal collection agency in Westchester. The first installment of the 2026 school tax was due September 30, 2026, so that deadline is behind you. Get the next due date and a written balance from the office before closing.

  • Checks are payable to the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes, 177 Hillside Avenue. Online card payments carry a variable fee, while ACH payments are free.
  • Liens cannot be paid online and must be settled at the Tax Office.
  • Last-day hours run to 7 p.m. on January 31, April 30 and September 30.
  • A new owner should call the tax office so future bills go to the right person.

Two state rules are quoted on the page. A bill that never arrives does not erase the tax or interest (Real Property Tax Law section 922), and the Receiver has no authority to waive a penalty (section 920). If you have moved out, send your new mailing address to the office in writing.

sections.h2: How does the Greenburgh assessment roll work?
sections.html:
The Assessment Rolls page says the tentative roll is open to the public by June 1. The Board of Assessment Review decides appeals until the roll becomes final on September 15, and that final roll is a snapshot that ignores later small claims changes. The page links the 2026 Final Assessment Roll as the current one.

Check your own line on the roll against what similar houses nearby sold for. A buyer's attorney will read the same record, and the Assessor's Office can answer questions about the latest figure.

sections.h2: What does the Westchester County Clerk need to record a Greenburgh deed?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk. Its recording guide lists four required pieces: a cover page made in the county's PREP system, a TP-584, an RP-5217 transfer report, and a payment cover page showing fees and tax.

The clerk gives the state transfer tax as $2 per $500 of price, rounding up to the next $500, and its example turns a $404,501 price into $1,620. Using the same math, a sale at the $697,100 median would owe about $2,790. Separately, a house or condo for one to three families conveyed at $1,000,000 or more owes a one percent mansion tax. The clerk's staff do not draft deeds or advise on them, so lean on your attorney for the document.

sections.h2: What should a Greenburgh seller prepare first?
sections.html:
• The property condition disclosure statement required by Real Property Law section 462, handed over before any binding contract is signed.
  • Certificates of occupancy or completion for any finished space, and permit records for recent work.
  • Town, county and school tax bills, plus a village bill if you live in a village.
  • A lender payoff letter and details of any lien.
  • Your STAR status: the state asks owners to close a registration after a sale.

faqs.q: Do village homes in Greenburgh use the town Building Department?
faqs.a: Generally not. The town department says it handles complaints in the unincorporated part of Greenburgh only. For a house in a village such as Tarrytown, ask the village hall about permits and due dates.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a new roof in Greenburgh?
faqs.a: Yes. A roof covering replacement on a one or two family house needs a building permit with drawings, and any structural change needs plans from a licensed architect or engineer.

faqs.q: Can the next owner run a short-term rental from a Greenburgh house?
faqs.a: The town says short-term rentals are not a permitted use in any residential zoning district. A buyer with that plan should confirm with the Building Department before closing.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a $700,000 Greenburgh sale?
faqs.a: State tax is $2 for every $500, which comes to $2,800 on $700,000. The one percent mansion tax starts at $1,000,000 for one to three family homes and condos.

faqs.q: Where do Greenburgh property tax payments go?
faqs.a: They go to the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes at 177 Hillside Avenue, which collects for the county, town, fire districts and ten school districts. Village residents follow their village's own schedule.
